title: Cooling Water Distribution System
model_title: Cooling Water Distribution System (Tower, Pumps, Headers, Users)

introduction.definition: A cooling water distribution system circulates water between a cooling tower and the plant's heat users. Pumps draw cold water from the tower basin and send it through supply headers to exchangers and condensers; warmed water returns to the tower, where a small part evaporates and cools the rest.
key_points: Make-up replaces evaporation, drift and blowdown
Water treatment controls scale, corrosion and biology
introduction.summary: A cooling water distribution system circulates water from a cooling tower to the plant's heat users and back. Pumps draw cold water from the tower basin and push it through a supply header to coolers and condensers; the warmed water returns to the tower, where evaporation cools it again.

temperature.title: Supply (cool) and return (warm) water
temperature.description: Water leaves the basin cool, picks up heat in the users and returns warmer to the tower. The temperature difference supply–return is the range (often ≈ 5–10 °C); how close the cold water gets to the air's wet-bulb temperature is the approach (often ≈ 3–6 °C). Evaporation, drift and blowdown losses are replaced by make-up water.

piping: Size headers for velocity ≈ 1.5–3 m/s; strainers before users; balancing valves; air release at high points.

video_tutorials.title: Cooling Water Distribution System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Cooling Water Distribution System.
A cooling water distribution system circulates water between a cooling tower and the plant's heat users.
Pumps draw cold water from the tower basin and send it through supply headers to exchangers and condensers; warmed water returns to the tower, where a small part evaporates and cools the rest.
Typical applications include power plants and refineries; chemical and manufacturing plants; HVAC chilled-water condensers.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Tower Fan, CW Pump 1 (duty), CW Pump 1 (duty) — Shaft & Coupling (turning), CW Pump 2 (standby).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Cooling Water Distribution System — Operation

script.narration: How the Cooling Water Distribution System works.
Cold water collects in the tower basin.
CW pumps send it into the supply header.
Users (coolers, condensers) pick up heat.
Warm water returns to the tower distribution.
Water falls through the fill; the fan draws air up and evaporation cools it.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Water leaves the basin cool, picks up heat in the users and returns warmer to the tower.

video_tutorials.title: Cooling Water Distribution System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Cooling Water Distribution System.
Check pumps, basin level, conductivity and chemical dosing.
Clean strainers; inspect fill and drift eliminators.
Overhaul pumps and fan gearboxes; inspect tower structure.
Watch for scaling/fouling of users: rising approach temperatures at exchangers. Common cause: high cycles of concentration, poor treatment.
Watch for legionella risk: positive samples. Common cause: stagnant water, warm temperatures, poor biocide control.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
